text: There is a short list of things you have never had to argue for with this person, and most of them are things you did not know could be argued. Pluto takes about two and a half centuries to get around the zodiac. Your Pluto on theirs means your two births sit close together on that very long circuit, close enough that you were handed the same sense of what is rotten and has to go. That agreement sits under the conversation rather than in it. When you say some arrangement is finished, that a thing built to last is hollow all the way through, they do not ask you to defend the premise. They start from it. Whatever the years around your birth decided would not be tolerated any longer, both of you took in as plain fact rather than opinion. Most people you deal with treat it as a position you have to make a case for. This person never does. The comfort in that is real, and easy to overvalue. You may find yourself thinking they understand you at a depth nobody else reaches. Some of that is accurate. Some of it is that the two of you are standing on the same ground and crediting the bond for the ground. This is the most common contact your Pluto can make with anyone else's, and you share it with a very large number of people neither of you has met. It is true about you both. It is not private. What you lose is a second opinion. Where your read on what must be destroyed is off, theirs is off in the same place, and neither of you is positioned to notice. If you both think some institution is past repair, nobody in the room will ask whether it might only be tired. If you both think a certain kind of pain is the price of anything worth having, that goes unchallenged too. Shared certainty is comfortable in exact proportion to how little it gets tested. Used well, the contact is a floor. You can skip a whole layer of explanation with this person and start work at the level where the real disagreements are. In a shared project it means you rarely fight about what the project is for. In a long friendship it means the hard subjects can be raised without a preface. That is worth something, particularly if you are the sort who usually has to soften what you actually think. Say plainly what this angle covers and what it does not. It reports that your two charts mark nearly the same point in Pluto's round, which is a fact about the calendar. It says nothing about how intense the two of you are with each other, who has more say, or what either of you does under pressure. Those questions live in other contacts, mostly the ones your Pluto makes with their Sun, Moon, or Venus, and theirs with yours. What you have here is a shared starting assumption about what cannot stay as it is, and a blind spot pointed in exactly the same direction.

A second account of what went wrong is on offer in this connection, and nothing obliges you to pick it up. Sixty degrees of Pluto's round separate your birth from theirs. That is a span of decades, though how many is not fixed: Pluto moves at very different speeds along its path, and it crosses some sixty-degree stretches in half the time it needs for others. What the distance produces is difference you can follow. Their sense of what has to be torn out is not yours, and it is close enough to yours to be legible. When they describe what they think has gone wrong with the world, you do not have to translate, and you do not have to defend your own version in order to hear theirs. That combination is uncommon. Most people either agree with you on this subject or set your teeth on edge. The use of it is quiet. Around this person, your own convictions about what must change stop looking like the weather and start looking like a view. Nobody has insulted you. They simply hold a different one, without apology, and yours turns out to be a position after all. That shift is hard to come by any other way, because people rarely stay calm long enough on this subject to hand it to you. In practice you will see it when something has to be judged. You say a situation is past saving. They neither nod along nor object. They hear it as one specific verdict, reached by a person with reasons, and they ask about the reasons. If you are the sort who settles these things fast and privately, being asked is a service. The same room runs the other way. What they consider unforgivable, you can take seriously without adopting, and that is rarer for them than they are likely to say. Nothing on either side presses. A sextile between two Plutos never demands anything, which is its main limit. You can find this person interesting for years, agree that they see something you do not, and never once bring them a decision you are actually facing. Then it stays a pleasant fact and does no work. About what the angle claims: it places your two charts sixty degrees apart on a very slow circuit, and that is the whole of it. It does not say which of you stands earlier in the round, how the distance cashes out in lived years, or anything at all about how either person behaves. It describes two different inherited ideas about what must be ended, set at a workable distance, with the trade left entirely up to the two of you.

Get to the bottom of a disagreement with this person and you often find it was never about the thing in front of you. Your Pluto squares theirs, a quarter turn on a circuit that needs roughly two hundred and fifty years to close. A gap that wide means the two of you inherited different ideas about where the real damage lies, and each of those ideas came with a matching idea about what has to be pulled down. So you can agree completely that something is broken and still get nowhere. You look at an arrangement and see a structure that has to go, whatever the cost of removing it. They look at the same arrangement and see the fix for a disaster you never had to live through, and the price you are willing to pay reads to them as recklessness. Turn the two views around and you have their side of it. Neither of you is arguing from a preference. Both of you are arguing from something that feels like knowledge. That is why the heat runs higher than the subject seems to warrant. Pluto is not the part of a chart that does moderation. When your Pluto and theirs stand at odds, what is in dispute is what counts as beyond saving, and neither of you can treat that as a matter of taste. You may notice you can concede a hundred smaller points to this person and not this one. They have the same experience from where they stand. Nobody chose any of it. The sky at your birth was not your decision, theirs was not theirs, and the friction between the two Plutos is a fact about how far apart the charts sit rather than a report on anyone's character. Reading it as character is the failure mode here, and it is an easy mistake, because it feels precisely like character while it is going on. There is traction in the arrangement. A square makes you state what you believe about power and about what it costs to change anything, and you will not be made to state it by someone who already agrees. Near this person your account of what is wrong has to be argued instead of assumed. What is left standing when the argument ends belongs to you differently than it did. Some of it will not survive, and that is the use of the thing. Read the angle honestly. It tells you the two births sit a quarter of Pluto's round apart. Because the planet's pace changes so much across its orbit, it does not tell you how many years that quarter turn covers. It tells you nothing about who is right, who gives way, or how either of you carries yourself when the argument gets old. All it names is a wide distance in a slow cycle, and the difference in premises that comes with the distance.

Nobody asks you to defend your sense of what has to change here, and you may not notice how unusual that is until you are somewhere else. Your Pluto trines theirs, which sets the two births a third of Pluto's whole round apart. That is a long stretch of the cycle, long enough that the two of you were not formed by the same alarms. Distance that wide normally produces argument. It does not in this case. Their idea of what is past fixing came out of a different set of events than yours, and it arrives as a variation rather than a challenge. You can hear it whole. They can hear yours the same way. Two people who take entirely different things for granted about power and its wreckage turn out not to be braced against each other, and that ease is usually the first thing you feel. What it buys you is scale. Most of what you are certain about on this subject you absorbed rather than chose, and it is close to impossible to see the edge of it from inside. This person shows you the edge without leaning on it. You get a look at another way the same problem was understood, in a form calm enough to actually consider. Something travels back the other way. Your version reaches them as coherent rather than naive or out of date, which is not how such things usually cross a gap this size. What strikes you as urgent gets treated by them as a serious position and not as a mood. Nothing in this angle plays the part of a corrective. Ease turns into admiration, and admiration across a wide span goes sentimental quickly. It is very easy to decide the other account of what went wrong runs deeper than yours simply because it is unfamiliar, or to give your own extra weight because they never push back on it. Neither of you supplies friction. For this contact to be worth more than a good feeling, one of you has to bring it a live question and let the answer come back inconvenient. Two limits, stated plainly. The angle reports that your Pluto and theirs sit a third of a round apart, and Pluto's speed varies enough that a third of a round is not a fixed number of years. And a contact between two Plutos describes assumptions, not people. Nothing in it says how either of you acts, how much either of you concedes, or what happens between you when something real is at stake. It says that on the question of what must not be left standing, you and they stand a long way apart and are not fighting about it.

Your Pluto and theirs face each other across the widest gap this contact can make: half of a round that takes about two hundred and fifty years to finish. Whatever your side of the cycle treats as the thing that cannot be allowed to continue, their side treats as the correction to some other problem, and the two charts hold opposite ends of one long argument about what must be destroyed and what must be kept. Positions get assigned fast. You become the one saying the whole structure has to come down. They become the one saying look what came of the last time somebody said that. Or the roles run the other way, and you are the one defending something whose cost you happen to know. Neither of you picked a side. The geometry handed them out before either of you could speak. Because this is an opposition rather than a square, the two views are not simply incompatible. They are two halves of one subject. What you understand about how things fall apart and what they understand are both true, and each is missing what the other holds. The completion is worth having and it does not feel good while it arrives. Being shown the far end of your own conviction is hard going, especially on the one question where you are least willing to be provisional. Watch for the pull toward the extremes. Facing a strong opposite tends to make people harder rather than more curious, and both ends of this axis can dig in until each is a caricature of itself. The angle makes that the cheapest available move and never an obligation. Then the plain part, because this is a contact that gets misread more than most. Half a round is an enormous distance in a very slow cycle. The angle tells you the two charts stand at opposite stations and tells you nothing else: not how that distance came about, not what either person is like, not who carries more weight in whatever passes between you. Charts get compared across long spans of time for many reasons, and the aspect does not name yours. What it describes is a full account of what must change, split down the middle, with your half in one chart and the rest of it in the other. Where the two halves are allowed to stay in the room together, the picture you end up with is wider than either chart carries alone.
